findings.label: The last unbeaten
findings.title: Ordway and Son has acquired the view from the top. The previous tenant lost by 2.88.
findings.body: Tranimal arrived at 3–0, a record which encourages a person to mistake four Sundays for a personality. Ordway and Son won 126.98–124.10 and took first place on season points. The family business had lost to McConkey Kong a week earlier; apparently the succession plan required a brief period of public embarrassment. Chuba Hubbard supplied 27.4, Romeo Doubs 20.8, and the league now has no undefeated teams. We can all resume speaking normally.

findings.label: The breakout
findings.title: Tet McMillan gave Cody a win worth discussing before the bench audit.
findings.body: After two straight losses, Caleb’s Elite Touch Rate beat Extremely Tight Ends 131.76–109.82. Tet McMillan supplied 40.2; Bryce Young added 21.46 from a quarterback slot belonging to a franchise still named for Caleb. There is a proper football story here before anyone opens the bench spreadsheet. Kyle Monangai’s 29.5 did stay unused, but winning does not require finding every available point. Cody is back at 2–2. Pete is there too, with 67.3 more season points and precisely the same number of wins.

findings.label: The jurisdiction
findings.title: Jerruh’s World has discovered that the visiting team retains certain rights.
findings.body: For two weeks Andrew’s franchise had been remarkably consistent: 126.88, then 127.84, and two wins. Gimothy Blossoms interrupted the arrangement with a 158.38–90.10 demolition. Bijan Robinson and Alvin Kamara supplied 51.5 between them. Kenneth Walker’s 34.4 was a substantial individual objection on the other side, but the court was not hearing individual objections. Alan has recovered from 0–2 to 2–2. Jerruh’s World has reached the same address by a less pleasant route.

findings.label: The first invitation
findings.title: De’Coldest Hassan has finally been admitted to the winners’ conversation.
findings.body: Mohsin lost the opener with 147.66 points, lost again with 129.20, then lost a third time with considerably less material for an appeal. His first win arrived with 110.68 against RFK Jr’s Bears. CeeDee Lamb contributed 34.8, and a season that had become rather tiresome to introduce is now 1–3. The Bears, meanwhile, have followed two wins with two losses. Nobody has changed tables quite as decisively as the standings suggest. They have simply had different Sundays.

findings.label: The working capital
findings.title: T. Ocellus bought the wrong headline and still made a useful investment.
findings.body: Bryan spent 17 FAAB on Kenyon Sadiq, then received zero from that starting slot. The more productive acquisition was Emanuel Wilson, added the previous week and worth 25.5 from FLEX in a 126.22–104.82 win over El Niño Grande. A transaction’s price is an expression of expectation; the scoreboard is under no obligation to respect it. Ocellus has won twice since starting 0–2. Corey has lost twice since starting 2–0. Both accounts now show 2–2, with very different recent statements.

findings.label: The rebrand
findings.title: Nix in 5 has won in four. Bo was not required to attend.
findings.body: Patrick’s first victory was a 143.38–112.44 win over McConkey Kong, achieved with the franchise’s namesake on the bench. Kyler Murray handled the quarterback shift; Nico Collins and Javonte Williams supplied 58.1 between them. A team called Nix in 5 going 0–3 had been allowing the public a little too much time to workshop the name. That period is over. Sandy falls to 2–2, joining seven other teams in a midtable gathering that has become larger than several actual parties.
findings.receipt: NIX IN 5: FIRST WIN • EIGHT TEAMS AT 2–2
